beats.say: A queue sells tickets, but the price climbs while you wait.
First card: standing spot at the lowest listed price.
Third: guaranteed seat at a higher fixed rate.
Standing tickets jump from £148.50 to £355. Nonsense.
But it's surge pricing, a hidden queue multiplier.
Ticketmaster spikes the price once the online line hits a threshold.
The 'in demand' option turns £148.50 into £355 after hours.
Cinemas add a 'peak' surcharge, £12 becomes £20 on busy nights.
Gyms list a 'high demand' plan, £30 jumps to £55 when classes fill.
The premium now feels cheap because the base surged.
If a price climbs while you wait, suspect a demand surge. Follow for more.
